curriculum.title: Planning and execution graphs
curriculum.outcome: Convert ambiguous goals into typed, bounded plans
curriculum.lesson:
Separate a goal into dependency nodes with explicit inputs, outputs, and verification gates; execute only ready nodes and record state transitions.

In the seminar, distinguish the trusted application policy from the model's probabilistic suggestions. Draw the complete data flow, identify which component owns state, and document the boundary of every external call. Derive an acceptance criterion before implementing the lab. Compare the smallest deterministic baseline with a tool-using alternative and capture a successful example, a controlled failure, and an observed trade-off. A convincing result requires traceable inputs and verification, not fluency alone.

Laboratory: Build a JSON task planner with topological ordering and a three-step budget. Failure analysis: Reject cyclic plans and tasks without an owner or exit condition. Finish by summarizing what changed under the failure condition and which checks were decisive.
objectives: Explain and diagram: Convert ambiguous goals into typed, bounded plans.
Build and test: Build a JSON task planner with topological ordering and a three-step budget.
Investigate failure: Reject cyclic plans and tasks without an owner or exit condition.
curriculum.assignment: Build a JSON task planner with topological ordering and a three-step budget. Deliver runnable code or a reproducible mock, architecture explanation, unit tests and the negative-case result. Include a pull request to your verified learner branch.
